> Read an mzLib spectral library (.msl) as one row per precursor, or with fragments one row per fragment ion, with mzLib's not-available sentinels as nulls.

Wire verb `library read` · Python [`pymzlib.library.read`][pymzlib.library.read]

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `path` | required | — | `.msl, any case (MslFileTypeHandler.IsMslFile)` | An mzLib binary spectral library. Any other extension is a usage error before the file is opened: text libraries (.msp) are not read by this verb. |
| `fragments` | `flag` | `false` | — | — | One row per fragment ion instead of one per precursor: the precursor's columns repeated on each row, then the fragment's. A precursor with no fragment ions gives one row whose fragment cells are null. Given with a value is a usage error. |
| `index_only_threshold` (wire `--index-only-threshold`) | `int` | `1073741824` | bytes | `>= 0` | Passed to MslFileTypeHandler.Open: a library this size or larger opens index-only (precursors in memory, fragment blocks read from disk on demand), a smaller one is loaded whole. Absent means mzLib's own default, MslFileTypeHandler.DefaultIndexOnlyThresholdBytes, 1073741824 bytes (1 GiB) at the pin; the bridge sends no value of its own. 0 opens every library index-only. The rows are the same in both modes; only memory and speed differ. |
| `offset` | `int` | `0` | precursors | `>= 0` | Skip this many precursors, in precursor_index order. A window, not a cursor: the library is opened again on every call. |
| `limit` | `int` | absent | precursors | `>= 0` | Return at most this many precursors; with fragments each gives one row per fragment ion. Absent means no limit. |
| `out` | `path` | absent | — | `.tsv only, any case (PYB-1)` | Write the table to this path as tab-separated text instead of returning columns. Must differ from path. Parent directories are created. Must end in .tsv, any case (PYB-1); any other extension, or none, is a usage error before the library is opened, and no extension is appended. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the library. |
| `file_type` | `string` | — | yes: always: .msl is not an mzLib SupportedFileType (mzLib reads it with MslLibrary, outside FileReader), so there is no type name to give | The mzLib SupportedFileType, for parity with the reader verbs. |
| `reader` | `string` | — | never | Always MslLibrary, the mzLib class that read the file. |
| `format_version` | `int` | — | never | The file's .msl format version (MslFileHeader.FormatVersion): 1 to 3 at the pin, where 3 allows compression (MslFormat.CurrentVersion). |
| `is_compressed` | `bool` | — | never | The fragment section is zstd-compressed (MslLibrary.IsCompressed). A compressed library always loads whole. |
| `is_index_only` | `bool` | — | never | mzLib opened the library index-only (MslLibrary.IsIndexOnly): at or above index_only_threshold, and not compressed. |
| `target_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Precursors that are not decoys, entrapment targets included (MslLibrary.TargetCount). |
| `decoy_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Decoy precursors, entrapment decoys included (MslLibrary.DecoyCount). |
| `proteoform_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Precursors whose molecule_type is Proteoform (MslLibrary.ProteoformCount). |
| `min_precursor_mz` | `float` | m/z | yes: the library has no precursors | Smallest precursor m/z (MslLibrary.MinPrecursorMz). |
| `max_precursor_mz` | `float` | m/z | yes: the library has no precursors | Largest precursor m/z (MslLibrary.MaxPrecursorMz). |
| `record_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Precursors in the whole library, before the window (MslLibrary.PrecursorCount). |
| `rows_not_read` | `int` | rows | yes: always: the file is binary and mzLib validates it whole (magic, version, footer, precursor count, CRC-32) before returning any entry, so every precursor is read or the call fails | Data rows that did not become records. |
| `retention_time_unit` | `string` | — | yes: always: the unit varies by precursor, so it is the retention_time_unit column | Always null for this verb. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | What this table cannot be trusted to mean, each citing the mzLib source. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | Column order. |
| `absent_fields` | `string[]` | — | never | Columns this library has no source for, from its file flags (MslFormat.FileFlag*): ion_mobility when no precursor has one, protein_accession and protein_name when there is no protein table, gene_name when there are no gene names. Null in every row (BULK.md section 4). |
| `failed_fields` | `string[]` | — | never | 'field: ExceptionType' for each column whose read threw on some returned rows; those cells are null. |
| `excluded_fields` | `object[]` | — | never | Always empty: every field crosses, the fragments with the fragments flag. |
| `error` | `object` | — | yes: always, for a single path: a library that cannot be read fails the call instead | {kind, type, message}; non-null only in a files[] entry under on-error skip. |
| `fragments_included` | `bool` | — | never | Whether the rows are fragment ions (the fragments flag). |
| `index_only_threshold` | `int` | bytes | never | The threshold MslFileTypeHandler.Open applied: the one given, or mzLib's default, 1073741824 at the pin. |
| `returned_count` | `int` | precursors | never | Precursors returned in columns (the unit offset and limit count in); 0 when written to out. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Rows in columns: returned_count without fragments, one per fragment ion (or one for a precursor with none) with them; 0 when written to out. |
| `offset` | `int` | precursors | never | The offset applied. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | — | never | True whenever precursors were left out by offset or limit. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | yes: the table was written to out instead | Column name to per-row values, in column_names order. |
| `output` | `object` | — | yes: out was not given | {path, format: "tsv", row_count} when out was given. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source_index` | `int` | — | never | 0-based position of the row's library in the stdin list. *Present only with `--paths-stdin`.* |
| `source_path` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the row's library. *Present only with `--paths-stdin`.* |
| `precursor_index` | `int` | — | never | 0-based position of the precursor in the library (MslPrecursorIndexEntry.PrecursorIdx): the key MslLibrary.GetEntry takes, and the row order. Not m/z order. |
| `full_sequence` | `string` | — | never | Modified sequence in mzLib bracket notation, e.g. PEPTM[Common Variable:Oxidation on M]IDE (MslLibraryEntry.FullSequence). |
| `base_sequence` | `string` | — | never | The bare residues (MslLibraryEntry.BaseSequence). |
| `precursor_mz` | `float` | m/z | never | Precursor m/z, (M + zH)/z (MslLibraryEntry.PrecursorMz), stored as a 32-bit float. |
| `charge_state` | `int` | charge | never | Precursor charge (MslLibraryEntry.ChargeState). |
| `retention_time` | `float` | iRT or min (per row) | never | Indexed retention time, or a run-calibrated time in minutes, as retention_time_unit says (MslLibraryEntry.RetentionTime). iRT can be negative. 0 is passed through: mzLib documents no sentinel for it. |
| `retention_time_unit` | `string` | — | never | iRT or minutes, from MslLibraryEntry.RtIsCalibrated (false: iRT; true: run-specific minutes). Per row because one library can hold both. |
| `ion_mobility` | `float` | 1/K0 (V s/cm2) | yes: mzLib's 0.0, which MslLibraryEntry.IonMobility documents as not available; in absent_fields when no precursor has one | Ion mobility as 1/K0 (MslLibraryEntry.IonMobility). |
| `is_decoy` | `bool` | — | never | A decoy precursor, entrapment decoys included (MslLibraryEntry.IsDecoy). |
| `is_entrapment` | `bool` | — | never | An entrapment precursor, target or decoy (MslLibraryEntry.IsEntrapment, mzLib #1383). Independent of is_decoy. |
| `decoy_contaminant_target` | `string` | — | never | T, D, ET or ED, from DecoyContaminantTargetLabel.For(is_decoy, false, is_entrapment). The .msl format has no contaminant flag, so C never appears. |
| `protein_accession` | `string` | — | yes: mzLib's empty string: the precursor has no protein (MslLibraryEntry.ProteinAccession); in absent_fields when the library has no protein table | Accession of the source protein, as stored, e.g. P04637. |
| `protein_name` | `string` | — | yes: mzLib's empty string: no protein, or no name for it (MslLibraryEntry.ProteinName); in absent_fields when the library has no protein table | Protein name, as stored. |
| `gene_name` | `string` | — | yes: mzLib's empty string: no protein, or no gene for it (MslLibraryEntry.GeneName); in absent_fields when the library has no gene names | Gene symbol, as stored, e.g. TP53. |
| `is_proteotypic` | `bool` | — | never | Expected to give a uniquely detectable signal (MslLibraryEntry.IsProteotypic), as the library's writer set it. |
| `q_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: mzLib's NaN: no q-value is available, as for a purely predicted library (MslLibraryEntry.QValue) | The library's q-value for the precursor; lower is better. |
| `elution_group_id` | `int` | — | never | Shared by every precursor of one base sequence, so charge states and modified forms co-elute (MslLibraryEntry.ElutionGroupId); mzLib's writer assigns it. |
| `molecule_type` | `string` | — | never | MslFormat.MoleculeType name: Peptide, Proteoform, Oligonucleotide or Glycopeptide. |
| `source_type` | `string` | — | never | MslFormat.SourceType name (MslLibraryEntry.Source): Predicted, Empirical, or EmpiricalRefined (predicted intensities, measured retention time or ion mobility). |
| `dissociation_type` | `string` | — | never | mzLib DissociationType name, e.g. HCD; Unknown when the library does not say (MslLibraryEntry.DissociationType). |
| `nce` | `int` | NCE | yes: mzLib's 0: unknown or not applicable (MslLibraryEntry.Nce) | Normalized collision energy, a whole number: the format stores NCE x 10 and mzLib divides by 10 as an integer. |
| `fragment_count` | `int` | fragment ions | never | Fragment ions the precursor has, counted from the ions mzLib read; 0 for a precursor with none, whose one row has every fragment cell null. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `fragment_mz` | `float` | m/z | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions (fragment_count 0) | Fragment m/z (MslFragmentIon.Mz), a 32-bit float. Rows are in the stored order, which mzLib's writer sorts by m/z. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `fragment_intensity` | `float` | relative intensity (0 to 1) | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | Intensity relative to the precursor's most intense fragment, which mzLib's writer scales to 1 (MslFragmentIon.Intensity). Not comparable across precursors. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `product_type` | `string` | — | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | mzLib ProductType name, e.g. b, y, c, zDot; for an internal ion, its N-terminal type (MslFragmentIon.ProductType). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `secondary_product_type` | `string` | — | yes: a terminal ion (MslFragmentIon.SecondaryProductType is null for every terminal ion), or no fragment ions | An internal ion's C-terminal ProductType, e.g. y for bIy. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `fragment_number` | `int` | — | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | The ion's number in its series, e.g. 5 for b5; for an internal ion, its 0-based start residue (MslFragmentIon.FragmentNumber). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `secondary_fragment_number` | `int` | — | yes: a terminal ion, for which mzLib stores 0 (MslFragmentIon.SecondaryFragmentNumber), or no fragment ions | An internal ion's end residue, exclusive. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `residue_position` | `int` | — | yes: mzLib's 0: always for a fragment with a custom neutral loss, whose stored position the format reuses to index its loss table (MslReader.ConvertFragment); or no fragment ions | Residue position the ion was annotated from, as stored (MslFragmentIon.ResiduePosition): for a library mzLib built from its own products, the Product.ResiduePosition convention, fragment_number for N-terminal ions and length - fragment_number + 1 for C-terminal ones (mzLib #1408). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `fragment_charge` | `int` | charge | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | Fragment charge (MslFragmentIon.Charge). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `neutral_loss` | `float` | Da | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | Neutral-loss mass, negative for a loss (MslFragmentIon.NeutralLoss). 0 means no loss, and crosses as 0, not null: it is the value of the shift, not a missing one. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `is_internal` | `bool` | — | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | An internal ion (MslFragmentIon.IsInternalFragment). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `is_diagnostic` | `bool` | — | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | A diagnostic ion, ProductType D (MslFragmentIon.IsDiagnosticIon). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `exclude_from_quant` | `bool` | — | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | Marked to be left out of quantification, like DIA-NN's ExcludeFromAssay (MslFragmentIon.ExcludeFromQuant). *Present only with `--fragments`.* |
| `annotation` | `string` | — | yes: the precursor has no fragment ions | mzLib's library rendering (MslFragmentIon.Annotation), e.g. b5, y3-18.0106, bIy[2-5] or y4^2+: the loss signed to four decimals and the charge appended, unlike Product.Annotation. *Present only with `--fragments`.* |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | path missing or blank; the file does not exist, or is a directory; its extension is not .msl (MslFileTypeHandler.IsMslFile) |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | fragments given a value; index-only-threshold, offset, limit or out given with no value; index-only-threshold not a whole number, or below 0; offset or limit below 0 or not an integer; out resolving to the same file as path |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | out (with path or paths-stdin) whose extension is not .tsv, any case, including none (PYB-1); checked before any input is opened |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | mzLib cannot read the library: FormatException for a bad magic number, version, footer or precursor count, InvalidDataException for a CRC-32 mismatch (MslReader); the error type is mzLib's exception name |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | paths-stdin with path, offset or limit; paths-stdin with a value; no paths on stdin; a repeated path; threads 0 or below -1; on-error not fail or skip; on-error skip with a single path; out naming an input |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | with on-error fail, an input that is missing or not a .msl: the usage error of that input, prefixed 'Input <i> (<path>)' |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | with on-error fail, mzLib failing to read an input: that input's own error type, message prefixed 'Input <i> (<path>)' |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | the answer is too large to return as one JSON document (PYB-3 part 1). Message: 'this read (N records) is too large to return as one document; use --limit/--offset or --out'. A library with fragments is the likeliest case: write it to out. |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- Rows are in the library's stored order, by precursor_index, not by m/z: mzLib's own MslLibrary.GetAllEntries enumerates in ascending precursor m/z instead. Sort on precursor_mz for that order.
- retention_time is iRT for some precursors and run minutes for others: read retention_time_unit on each row (MslLibraryEntry.RtIsCalibrated). A library can hold both, so never plot or compare the column without it. There is no conversion: iRT becomes minutes only through a calibration against a run.
- The library is unfiltered: decoys (D, ED) and entrapment precursors (ET, ED) are rows. Filter on is_decoy, or on decoy_contaminant_target, before counting targets.
- A retention_time of 0 may mean the source had none: MslLibraryEntry.FromLibrarySpectrum, the path mzLib converts a text library through, writes RetentionTime ?? 0.0, and mzLib documents no sentinel for it, so 0 is passed through as a value.
- nce is a whole number: the format stores NCE x 10 and MslReader reads it back with integer division, so an NCE of 27.5 reads as 27.
- A library converted from a text library (.msp) has no NCE, dissociation type, q-value, ion mobility or protein: LibrarySpectrum has no field for them, and MslLibraryEntry.FromLibrarySpectrum fills mzLib's not-available defaults, so nce and q_value are null and dissociation_type is Unknown.
- precursor_mz, retention_time and ion_mobility are stored as 32-bit floats and widened to double by mzLib, so 465.74 reads back as 465.739990234375. The extra digits are the float, not a measurement; round them for display.
- offset and limit count PRECURSORS. With fragments, each precursor gives one row per fragment ion.
- With fragments: residue_position is null for every fragment with a custom neutral loss, because the .msl format reuses that field to index its loss table and MslReader reads it back as 0.
- With fragments: fragment_intensity is relative within its precursor, 0 to 1, because mzLib's writer scales each precursor's most intense fragment to 1 (MslWriter). It is not comparable across precursors.
- Index-only (at or above index_only_threshold) keeps memory to the precursors, but with fragments every fragment block is read twice from disk: once to count the rows, once to write them. mzLib keeps each precursor's stored fragment count private, so the bridge cannot size the table without reading them.

### Example

```python
library = pymzlib.library.read('myPrositLib.msl')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`library_read_prosit.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/library_read_prosit.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

```python
library = pymzlib.library.read('synthetic_library.msl')
```

Recorded from the live bridge as [`library_read_synthetic.json`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/pyMzLib/blob/main/pkg/python/tests/fixtures/library_read_synthetic.json). The doctests in the API reference replay these recordings in CI.

!!! warning "Not yet verified"

    - Text libraries (.msp, pDeep, ms2pip) could be read through the same table: mzLib's MslConverter.FromMspFile parses one into an in-memory MslLibrary. Left out of v1 because the conversion fills not-available defaults for every field LibrarySpectrum lacks, and because SpectralLibrary picks the text dialect from the file name. Revisit on demand.
    - fragment_count is carried only with fragments: without them mzLib's index-only entries have an empty fragment list (MslLibrary.GetEntry(i, false), 'do not rely on MatchedFragmentIons being empty or full'), and the stored MslPrecursorRecord.FragmentCount is not public. A public count would give the precursor table this column at no I/O cost (PUSH-TO-MAINLAND).
    - No decoy filter is offered: MslLibrary.GetAllEntries(includeDecoys: false) has one, but GetAllEntries yields m/z order with no index, so the bridge reads by index and the caller filters on is_decoy. A GetAllEntries overload with includeFragments, or one that yields the index, would let the bridge wrap it directly.
